title: Retrodictive billing for merged multipart requests
creator: Naomi Kerr
description:
Problem: We observe cases where multipart requests (clients that stream chunks, retries, or late attachments) are merged inside the routing layer into a single server-side execution when fragments arrive within a short window. When that merge happens after the initial partial accounting pass, token credits are sometimes attributed to the merged execution rather than the original client request footprint. This results in (1) overcharging the surviving session, (2) orphaned credits for the earlier partials, or (3) inconsistent quota enforcement for rate-limited customers.

Scope: This ticket implements a retrodictive billing adjustment flow that: (a) tracks fragment provenance for merge candidates, (b) creates reversible provisional ledger entries on first-pass accounting, (c) performs a merge reconciliation step to deterministically assign final token attribution, and (d) issues backfill or debit transactions that are idempotent and auditable. Does not include UI work for exposing backfills to customers (follow-up PM ticket).

Why different from existing work: Many prior tickets focus on streaming idempotency, finalization semantics, or checkpointing. This work centers on a retrodictive adjustment pipeline that runs after merge decisions and interacts with quota enforcement and rate limiter state. The complexity arises from concurrent merges, long tail fragment arrival (seconds to minutes), and the need to avoid creating transient negative quotas or double-charges when retries replay fragments from the client.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end test harness that simulates: interleaved multipart sends, delayed attachments, duplicate fragments, and merge-by-time-window — and asserts that final per-session token tallies match ground-truth histogram generated by the harness.
2) Ledger semantics: every provisional charge has a linked final adjustment (backfill or debit) with idempotent reconciliation keys; audit trail entries include original fragment IDs, merge-ID, and reconciliation reason.
3) Quota enforcement: rate limiter never grants negative available tokens after reconciliation; customers never lose more than one charging cycle worth of credits due to a merge.
4) No change to existing streaming latency SLOs for non-merged flows (benchmark before/after within 5% variance).
5) Observability: new dashboard panel shows reconciled adjustments over time and a per-merge histogram; alerts when reconciliation rate > 0.5% of streaming sessions for 15min.
6) Release notes and an internal playbook describing how to investigate backfill spikes and trigger manual reversals for legacy cases.
suggested_solution:
1) Add a lightweight fragment provenance header in the session metadata (merge-key and fragment-id).
2) During initial accounting, create provisional ledger entries tagged as 'provisional:<recon-id>' and increment a provisional counter instead of finalizing quota debits.
3) After the routing layer decides to merge two or more execution streams into merge-id M, run a reconciliation worker that: aggregates fragment token counts, applies attribution rules (prefer earliest fragment owner; deterministic tie-break by request-id hash), issues final ledger entries 'final:<recon-id>' and reverses provisional entries where necessary.
4) Integrate reconciliation with the token rate limiter: apply a transient hold when provisional debits would violate hard quota; allow reconciliation to adjust the hold.
5) Ensure reconciliation worker is idempotent by using recon-id, merge-id, and a monotonic reconciliation sequence; persist reconciliation state in the audit log store.
6) Add end-to-end integration tests and a canary rollout for the reconciliation worker behind a runtime flag.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming session A that sends fragments f1 (100 tokens) then stalls.
2) Start session B that sends fragments g1 (50 tokens) and g2 (200 tokens) within the merge window; routing merges A and B into execution M.

3) Observe provisional ledger entries for f1, g1, g2 created at initial pass.
4) Without retrodictive reconciliation, final token tally may attribute all tokens to M or keep double entries; reproduce by replaying fragments from a test harness and inspect ledger.
comments: 2026-03-10 Naomi Kerr: Created ticket after oncall reported two customer invoices with unexplained extra tokens following a truncated client that retried a multipart upload.

2026-03-11 Diego Alvarez: Spike reproduced in local harness; confirmed merge happens in router when fragments arrive within 2s window. Observed provisional credits not being reconciled. Added integration test scaffold.

2026-03-12 Design review (triage): trade-off between earliest-owner attribution vs proportional attribution. PM prefers earliest-owner to keep semantics simple for customers; noted edge where earliest owner had retried fragments resulting in inflated counts — added tie-break rule by request-id hash.

2026-03-12 Engineering notes: Implemented provisional ledger prototype and reconciliation worker skeleton. Need to coordinate with rate-limiter team to avoid transient overdraw. Filing ENG-953422 as follow-up to extend quota-visible auditing endpoints.

2026-03-13 Diego Alvarez: Running canary on staging with flag 'reconciliation_v1' enabled for 5% of streaming traffic. No regressions in SLOs observed in preliminary metrics. Will run longer soak and create PR for ledger change.
